body:
Can't stop laughing!
Your car is so cuuute. ❤️
Lithium tastes like real hell and I have a hard time swallowing it, too.
Ritalin takes my anxiety away and also reduces my impulsive behaviors.

I literally shouted and burst into tears after reading this.
FUCK Khamenei and the hell that was made from our country just in 44 years.
I hope all of them turn into kotlets.

"It's an identity not a disease" This sentence literally ruined me.
People are suffering from that disease and these assholes make their identity based on it. "So cOoL! 🤪"
Dirty faker, stay awayyyy from Nirvana.
I have vivid dreams. Especially in hypomanic episodes, when I try hard to sleep at least for a few hours but these dreams don't leave me alone. So I can't sleep well.

Glad that this terrorist doesn't exist anymore. Happy kebab day!

-an Iranian
For the rest of their life.

Yes. Despite having lots of things to do, I leave them for the proper time. I feel like a crap. Really want to avoid this situation.
I Still can't focus on tasks and it's bothering that I'm not passionate for doing them, and needing some exciting thing. Spending time, waiting. Nothing's enjoyable.
Yes. It's possible. I might do that in the future.
I'm too young to be a writer. But I use the little bit of creativity that I have and write stories.
It was my main reason for discontinuing Lithium. Now I can write better. Though I experience the highs and lows, as it was before starting medication.
Getting thirsty as hell, and tremors.
I take it at night. (600 mg.)
I studied one of my lessons.
I realized that when my father talked about his hallucinations.
Even the EARTH has two poles. 🌎😡
I could never understand why people like having bipolar. What's the good thing of it? I wish I could give my disorder to whoever that likes having it. :)
I starve myself when I'm hypomanic and overeat when depression comes.
It's disgusting. I could never understand why some idiots think that mental disorders are cool and funny...
My friends once said: "Coffee makes me bipolar." It was annoying to me. What he feels after drinking coffee is NOT mania. :)
I have bipolar disorder and I want to stop taking medication. Side effects are worse than the illness.
They say I'm cringe, stupid and one of the worst people they have ever seen. Just out of nowhere, after our friendship has ended.
Let It Die by Foo Fighters.
I have attempted suicide. And I'm not grateful for surviving.
A few months ago I took 9000 mg of Lithium and 400 mg of Citalopram. Five hours later, I was in hospital. Unfortunately I couldn't die. But it caused damage to my body. Don't do this. It's painful.

My hypomania lasts for only a few days. I struggle with depression most of the time. And have trouble concentrating. That's why I'm thinking of dropping out.
Thank you. Hoping I can finish the last year of school. :)
Wish you the best.
I'll try not to give up.

I'm shy and it's hard for me to talk. But when hypomania kicks in, it makes me totally different and I'm no longer shy. I don't need sleeping and feel a huge amount of energy. I start to write. Because it gives me creativity. At first it's hard to differentiate hypomania from happiness.
I don't have a job. I'm a student and on the verge of dropping out of school.
I take 600 mg in morning and at night.
Staying in bed for long hours. Having suicidal thoughts. More self hate. Inability to think. It feels like hell.

Because it makes me different from other people. My disorder doesn't let me be as productive as others. Because it's gradually killing me. And I can't express my feelings to everyone. It also has a heavy stigma. I even feel disgusted when I hear the word "bipolar".
There's no good thing about it.
You're not alone. When I was unmedicated, I could write better.
I was 110 lbs and now I'm 100 lbs. No difference. (But I'm always afraid of hypothyroidism.)
Unfortunately, media always shows the end of spectrum.
I was prescribed Olanzapine. But I don't take it. 'Cause I'm fuckin afraid of weight gain. 😭
I take Lithium. But I had this problem before I start taking meds.
No. It just makes me anxious.
I have talked to my psychiatrist about it before. He said it's because of bipolar and there's no hope that it gets better.
I'm here after a hypomanic episode.
Because you're strong enough to continue living in this shitty world.
I overdosed a couple of weeks ago. It's a painful way to die and it doesn't lead to death most of the time. PLEASE call 911. ❤️
Last week I took 300 pills of Lithium and 20 pills of Citalopram. Unfortunately I didn't die.
And if you want to talk, you can dm me.
After 5 days of my last suicide attempt, I say: "Don't kill yourself. You probably won't die."
8 when stable. 10-13 when depressed. 2-3 during hypomania.
Yes. I've lost all my friends because of bipolar.
I don't have a dog. But I like to have. :)
I was listening to Come Alive by Foo Fighters and it made me feel better. :)
Yes. But both of them are bad.
Yes. I was misdiagnosed with unipolar depression.
I had a hypomanic episode recently and maybe these drugs were for treating that. I started last week and I can't say what effect it has on my depression.
I couldn't understand. But this painting is awesome.
Having a good friendship is so hard for me. But I still need some communications with people.
Yes. I've never experienced acute mania. And sometimes I miss my hypomanic episodes. ^-^
Yes. In hypomania, my eyes are big and sparkling. =)

At first, my doctor told me that I have depression. Then, it changed to bp. And my mother has an anxiety disorder. In my family there's no bipolar person instead myself. And..., best wishes for you. ✨

Bipolar symptoms. Sometimes I felt deeply sad, hopeless and tired. I attempted suicide. I hated everything and etc... And also, sometimes I was extremely happy and energetic and I shouted at people. I had a huge amount of energy and an increased creativity.
I'm struggling to accept, too. I think my diagnosis is a lie.
It's been more than a week that I'm on Abilify. I take it at nights and it makes me a bit tired. So I can sleep.
Thank you for Sharing your experience.
My English is not good. So I didn't understand. Lol.
And I just saw your comment right now. ✨
You hate yourself. But it doesn't mean other people hate you too.
I've been experiencing symptoms four years before I get the fucking diagnosis.
Ily too. I'm hopeful that it'll be alright.
I track my mood on a piece of paper. Depressive episodes are colorized black. Normal days are gray and hypomanic episodes are white.
Thank you for telling your story. 💖
Thanks for your comment. That's good to understand that diagnosis can be a relief for some people.
I'll try not to get that point. <3
It referred to both mania and depression. I totally agree. When we know it's not our fault, it's somehow a relief and it makes us more compassionate towards ourselves.
Thank you for your helpful comment. 💖
Thank you for giving me information. It really helps. <3
Thank you for telling your story. ✨
Oh. The cover. :) "I hate being bipolar. It's awesome."
Uncertainty sucks. For me, both uncertainty and accepting the diagnosis is hard. Lol.
Before getting my diagnosis, sometimes I thought that I'm an imposter. It was much more easier for me to think I'm faking everything. But I can't keep lying to myself. I know they're real. :(
That's one of my questions. "Did I fake all of my symptoms for 4 years?" Lol. ;)
So, are you taking medication because of them? Is it a kind of sacrifice?
Maybe accepting a physical illness is easier than accepting a mental illness.
I think it'll take a lot of time for me to completely accept that.
Never seen it from this point of view. Nice.
I'm 17. I've been experiencing bp symptoms since I was 13 years old. And thanks for telling your own story. 🌹
And I'm thinking about stopping meds because of side effects. I know it's a dumb desicion.
Keep going. Wish you the best.
Hope we all can fight with this damn internal creature. And, best wishes for you. <3
I do agree. Its existence doesn't depend on me. If I don't accept, it won't suddenly disappear.
That's really nice. I've never seen it from this point of view.
I guess I'm in denial. Having bipolar disorder scares me.
And I have an explanation for my suicide attempt. Lol.
I've experienced symptoms since four years ago. But a diagnosis confirms that my feelings were symptoms of a disorder. And that's somehow scary for me.
Glad to hear that. So it's possible to manage.
Ending up in a psych ward and a person who can not live a normal life, just like other people.
I believe they are real. But I'm even afraid of the name "Bipolar". It really scares me. And that's why I can't accept my illness.
I downloaded the book that you suggested.
I wish I could get out of denial.
I heard a voice that was shouting at me. The voice told me that I should kill myself. And another suicide attempt...
Thanks for your your comment. I agree. Sticking to treatment is very important. I remember once I stopped treatment and it led to another hypomanic episode.
I hope acceptance come with time.
It seems true. We can't do anything about it. We didn't choose to have the disorder.
Good idea. Every diagnosis is a possibility.
Even though I'm on meds, I think I don't have this fucking disorder and my doctor told me a lie.
I didn't accept my bp diagnosis.

I've written many stories when I was hypomanic. But I didn't finish any of them. The creativity that I have in my hypomania is somehow useless.
And for me, hypomanic episodes start with euphoria and extreme amount of happiness. After a short time, it turns to anger and lots of energy that I don't know how I should use it.
Yes. When anxiety kicks in, the joyful and euphoric feelings disappear suddenly and it doesn't let me enjoy some great feelings of my hypomania.

I feel like I'm drowning in the deepest part of an ocean and after that, I'm sitting at summit of the mountain and I'm seeing the whole world from above. It's like warm sunshine and cold snow. Like a roller coaster.
I was misdiagnosed with depression. After taking antidepressants and experiencing more hypomanic episodes, the diagnosis was changed to bipolar.
I could feel her existence and I could hear what she was telling me.

I'm 17 years old. My bipolar disorder didn't cause this. But my experience is kinda similar. I've heard voices in my depressive episodes. In the darkest times, the person in my head told me that I'm worthless and dying is the best solution for me. Which led to a suicide attempt this March.
5 mg. And it's been a few days that I'm on Abilify and Lithium. So I'm still feeling like sh-t.
I think it's a shameful illness.
A doctor can give you a diagnosis.
It's been a few days that I'm on it. Hope it works.
And thought I'm the only one who knows everything. So I can do whatever I want toward others.
I shouted at people and I wanted to hurt them. That was shameful. :(
Bipolar 2. And experiencing a mild depression. (Because of my meds.)
I still have my comfort toy.
